headline.title: Sam Altman responds to ‘incendiary’ New Yorker article after attack on his home
headline.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman addressed concerns raised in a New Yorker profile questioning his trustworthiness, following an incident where his home was attacked. In a blog post, he responded to the article's claims and the impact of the attack on his personal safety.

articles.title: Your article about AI doesn’t need AI art
articles.summary: The New Yorker's profile of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman features an unsettling illustration that includes disembodied faces resembling Altman, evoking a range of emotions. The artwork has drawn attention for its eerie portrayal, contrasting with the article's content.

articles.title: My baby deer plushie told me that Mitski’s dad was a CIA operative
articles.summary: The article discusses a friend's surprising text about singer Mitski's father allegedly being a CIA operative, prompting a reflection on the nature of such claims. It highlights the blend of personal anecdotes and cultural commentary surrounding the artist's background.

articles.title: How Iran out-shitposted the White House
articles.summary: The article discusses how Iranian state media effectively utilized social media to disseminate real-time footage of events during the conflict, contrasting this with the White House's less impactful online presence, which included memes and AI-generated content. This strategy allowed Iran to dominate the narrative in the digital space during the early stages of the war.

articles.title: Your Push Notifications Aren’t Safe From the FBI
articles.summary: The FBI has the capability to access and monitor push notifications, raising concerns about user privacy and security. Additionally, Iran's internet blackout has surpassed 1,000 hours, and cryptocurrency scams have led to a record amount of financial losses for Americans.

articles.title: How the Internet Broke Everyone’s Bullshit Detectors
articles.summary: The article discusses the challenges faced by verification systems in distinguishing real from fake content online, particularly in light of advancements in AI-generated images and restricted satellite data. It highlights the growing difficulty for individuals to trust the authenticity of information in the digital landscape.

articles.title: 20-year-old man arrested for allegedly throwing a Molotov cocktail at Sam Altman’s house
articles.summary: A 20-year-old man has been arrested by San Francisco police for allegedly throwing a Molotov cocktail at OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's house early Friday morning. The incident was captured on surveillance cameras, and the suspect was later seen making threats outside OpenAI's headquarters.

articles.title: Anthropic temporarily banned OpenClaw’s creator from accessing Claude
articles.summary: Anthropic has temporarily banned the creator of OpenClaw from accessing its AI model, Claude, following a recent change in pricing for OpenClaw users. The decision comes in response to concerns related to the new pricing structure implemented last week.
